content.comment_body: When attempting to set up a Network input, I enter the slave IP and input number, but clicking OK does nothing; my only choice is to cancel and abandon the setup. I couldn't find any resources explaining this issue, and there’s no error message displayed.
Has this issue persisted across all your projects, or only this specific one? What operating system are you using?

Although I've worked with [product_name] and LCS software for several years, I'm new to the ethernet interface. I managed to get the NI block working, but only under unusual conditions—I had to convert the code from ladder to logic block format, transfer it, read it back, and only then could I assign a slave status with an IP address. I thought perhaps my software had a bug. Is there something I might be overlooking?

Hello, I believe this behavior is atypical. I haven’t encountered issues using the NI Block, particularly with Function Block Diagram (FBD) rather than ladder. I insert the Network Input into the circuit diagram, access the Block Properties, select Slave, input the Slave IP, choose In- or Output, and pressing OK completes the process smoothly. I also tested this in ladder format and faced no problems. I use [product_name] V[version_no] and Windows XP SP3. If no other forum users have suggestions, contacting technical support from [company_name] might be best.

In ladder, insert the network input, open its properties, then enter the slave IP address and input number. Add a make contact, select network input from the list, and it should function correctly. I tested this and it worked for me.

I followed those steps and had the experience I described earlier. I spoke with [company_name] technical support, and it was unfamiliar to them as well, but they confirmed that I executed everything correctly.
Hi, I also work exclusively in FBD, but this procedure should work even if you prefer ladder logic.

Hello, I experienced a similar issue. I had a ladder project developed for [article_no], opened it, and converted it to [article_no]. Afterward, when trying to add a Network Input as Slave, pressing OK wasn’t possible. The solution was to create a fresh ladder project for [article_no] and copy everything from the converted [article_no] program. After this, the Network Inputs worked. The challenge is in copying—all output blocks (coils, timers, counters, etc.) should be copied first, then the rest of the program.
When you say you 'converted it to [article_no],' do you mean you switched the module by double-clicking the icon at the bottom? I haven’t yet tried copying the program—that sounds tedious! Thanks!

I recreated my program in a new file, and now it works. Thanks so much for the suggestion! I’m not sure what in the software blocked the previous method—perhaps there is an internal tag that records which software version originally authored the code? That’s the only difference I can think of.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered difficulties configuring Network Inputs within ladder logic using [product_name], especially when converting projects from older hardware ([article_no]) to newer ones ([article_no]). The main issue was being unable to save settings, with no error messages. Recreating the project in a fresh file resolved this, implying possible compatibility issues between converted and new files.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to set up Network Inputs seamlessly in both new and converted project files, and for the software to provide clear instructions or feedback when issues occur.
